## Summary

Fn-Link is a Chinese maker of wireless communication modules, founded
in 2015, whose catalogue lists 2.4G and 5G Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth
modules, Wi-Fi 6 modules, Wi-Fi BLE IoT modules, Bluetooth modules,
Cat.1 modules and Wi-Fi dongles, and whose stated solutions span IEEE
802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax, Bluetooth, Cat.1bis, PLC, Sub-1G and Zigbee [2].
The IEEE registry gives HUNAN FN-LINK TECHNOLOGY LIMITED an address on
Litong Road in the Liuyang economic and technical development zone,
Changsha, and lists blocks under FN-LINK TECHNOLOGY LIMITED and FN-LINK
TECHNOLOGY Ltd. as well, some at the same Litong Road address and
others in Shenzhen [1]. The company's own site gives a Shenzhen address
and names Huawei, Haier, Xiaomi, Midea, Hisense, Gree, Hikvision,
Skyworth and Ecovacs among its customers [2].

A MAC in an Fn-Link block is most likely the radio module inside
another brand's product rather than an Fn-Link product: a Victron Cerbo
GX owner found his controller listed as HUNAN FN-LINK on his router and
concluded that the name is the Wi-Fi adapter maker's, though Victron
did not confirm the cause [4]. Fn-Link's 6223E-UUD datasheet documents
a Realtek RTL8723DU, 802.11b/g/n 1T1R with Bluetooth 2.1+EDR, 3.0 and
4.2, over USB [3].

Randomization depends on the host device's operating system and no
source consulted documents it. FCC grantee codes are not listed: the
FCC ID databases refused the session that verified this entry, and
nothing is filled in from memory. Parent company and security
advisories are not documented by the sources consulted.
